data.long_meaning: Paresh is a Sanskrit name that derives from the term 'Para-ishwar', meaning 'Lord of all beings'. In Hindu mythology, this name is associated with the supreme deity, Lord Shiva. The name Paresh carries the meaning “Lord of all beings” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Paresh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of all beings and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Paresh carries deep cultural significance in Hinduism. This name is rooted in the belief that there is a supreme being who rules over all creation. This reverence for the divine is reflected in the naming tradition, where a child is given a name that reflects this belief. The use of the term 'Lord of all beings' underscores the importance of devotion, reverence, and respect for the divine in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Paresh is a constant reminder of the ultimate reality of the supreme deity. The name is believed to bestow blessings of divine protection, strength, and wisdom upon the bearer. It is a name that inspires one to connect with the divine and to live a life that is in harmony with the supreme consciousness. vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit word परिशत् (parishat), meaning 'army, retinue', which can also be interpreted as 'those who are near (to the king) and obey his commands'. The name Paresh can thus be seen as a reflection of the power and authority of a king or ruler.
